title: Get started
subtitle: Add Chaotic-AUR to pacman in five steps, then learn how builds and reviews work.

importKey.title: Import the primary key
importKey.text: Retrieve and locally sign the primary key. It lets pacman trust our keyring and mirror list.

install.title: Install packages
install.text: The repository is ready to use.

reportingBugs.text: Report package bugs to our bug tracker or comment on the AUR first. Report upstream only after you confirm that the issue is not a packaging issue. This gets bugs fixed faster.

deployLog.outro: shows whether a package was deployed after its last AUR update.

packageBuilds.reportFailures: Report build failures or broken packages as an issue in our GitHub repository.
packageBuilds.mainRepository: Our main repository is on GitLab, because the build system uses its CI pipelines extensively.

requestingNewPackages.text: Submit package requests as an issue in our GitHub repository. We prefer GitHub for historical reasons, so requests on GitLab can go unnoticed.
requestingNewPackages.searchIssues: Search the existing issues. We possibly handled or removed the package before, for a reason.
requestingNewPackages.license: Make sure that the license permits redistribution.
requestingNewPackages.banList: Make sure that the package is not on our ban list.

recommendations.ignoreUpdates: To keep a locally built version of a package (for example with native optimizations), ignore its updates in /etc/pacman.conf:
recommendations.specificRepository: To install a package from a specific repository, prefix it with the repository name:
recommendations.aurHelpers: AUR helpers like paru support the same syntax:

updateReviewProcess.mergeRequests: Some AUR updates change more than pkgver, pkgrel or checksums. For these, our build system opens a merge request against the pkgbuilds repository. Packages that build from a git branch update automatically when only their upstream commit changes. The state branch tracks these commits. AUR updates that change the PKGBUILD are the exception.
updateReviewProcess.humanApproval: The system flags suspicious changes automatically. Then a maintainer inspects each diff for malicious changes. A merge request is merged and deployed only after a human approves it.

scanner.intro: Screen AUR packages before you install them with our
scanner.outro: . It fetches the PKGBUILD and its sources and inspects them with our static security rules.

aurPackageScan.insights: It also shows maintainer insights, such as novice maintainers and orphaned packages. Always read the source code and PKGBUILD before you install a package. The scanner shows them next to the findings.
